title: Loading a prefix of the row
statement: Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an input-head position for $x$. Suppose $old$ and $new$ assign a binary word to each of the $l$ fields, with old-word lengths at most $U$ and new-word lengths at most $W$. For any binary prefix and trailer and every $j\le l$, the row loader started at field zero with the old fields and the stream containing the prefix, packed new fields, and trailer reaches in some time $t\le j(2U+3W+7)$ a configuration at field index $j$, with fields below $j$ replaced by their new words and the rest still old, and with the stream cursor immediately after the packed first $j$ new fields.
hypotheses_covered: old and new assign words to the $l$ fields
each old word has length at most $U$
each new word has length at most $W$
replaced: For every input word, input position, old fields of length at most $U$, new fields of length at most $W$, stream prefix and trailer, and count $j \le l$, there is a time $t \le j\,(2U + 3W + 7)$ after which the row loader, started at field zero with the stream holding the packed new row, has loaded exactly the first $j$ new fields, restored every field head to zero, and advanced the stream cursor by the exact length of the packed first $j$ fields. Every field is reset even when revisiting a short row after a longer one.
